analysis.investment_thesis: Fabtech is a small-cap proxy on India's pharma/biotech capex cycle with decent ROCE (21.2%) and clean balance sheet (borrowings just INR 10 Cr vs equity INR 95 Cr), but revenue at INR 150 Cr with lumpy turnkey-project economics and weak cash conversion keeps it in the "watch, don't back the truck" bucket. At 27.6x P/E for an 11% 5Y revenue CAGR business, the valuation already prices in execution I haven't yet seen.
key_strengths: Pharma cleanroom capex — structural tailwind from PLI and CDMO buildout in India
ROCE 21.2%, ROE 18.1%, promoter holding a healthy 68.49% — skin in the game
FY25 inflection: revenue +55% (97→150 Cr), PAT +117% (6→13 Cr), post-IPO equity of 95 Cr funds growth
key_risks: Weak cash conversion: FY25 OCF of just INR 3 Cr vs PAT INR 13 Cr — classic EPC working-capital leakage
Tiny scale (INR 270 Cr m-cap, INR 150 Cr sales) in a lumpy order-book business — one slippage kills a year
Only ~1 year of listed history post-IPO — promoter governance and capital allocation discipline unproven
red_flags: OCF (3 Cr) materially below net profit (13 Cr) — profit quality needs watching
Investing outflow of 26 Cr in FY25 funded almost entirely by IPO proceeds — execution on that deployment is the whole thesis
analysis.detailed_analysis: The sector is right — India's pharma industry is in a multi-year capex upcycle driven by PLI, CDMO outsourcing from the West, and biotech scale-up, and turnkey cleanroom engineering is a direct pick-and-shovel play. The numbers are also directionally attractive: FY25 saw revenue jump from 97 to 150 Cr, PAT more than doubled to 13 Cr, ROCE is 21.2%, and borrowings remain tiny at 10 Cr against 95 Cr equity after a post-IPO raise. Promoter at 68.49% is a big tick — in India, I always want founders holding >50% and aligned.\n\nBut I have hesitations. This is a project-based EPC-style business, and the cash flow statement betrays it — OCF of 3 Cr against reported PAT of 13 Cr in FY25, and 5Y cumulative OCF of ~INR 21 Cr against 5Y cumulative PAT of ~INR 36 Cr. That is classic working-capital-heavy turnkey economics. Combine that with tiny scale (150 Cr revenue), a single-year revenue spike that could easily be order-timing, an unproven listed track record, and a 27.6x multiple that already embeds strong growth — this is a "earn the position" stock, not a high-conviction bet. I would track 2-3 quarters of execution, watch receivables days, and size up only if the order book compounds and cash follows profit.
